voyage.name: Hangang Citizen's Park
voyage.content: Alongside the Han River through 13 districts: Gwangnaru, Jamsil, Gangdong, Ttukseom, Jamwon, Banpo, Ichon, Yeouido, Yanghwa, Mangwon, Seonyudo, Nanji, and Gangseojigu. You can see many people strolling or jogging along the trail paths, as well as in-line skaters, bicyclists, and soccer fields or basketball courts. Yeouido, Jamsil, and Ttukseom districts are especially popular because of the cruise services on the Han

voyage.name: National Museum of Korea
voyage.hours: For class times, inquire in advance

voyage.name: Cheonggye Stream
voyage.content: This stream has been restored to a verdant tourist attraction after long being covered by a busy freeway. You can walk many kilometers along its path through the very center of Seoul. Be cautious during the rainy day, because it may be flooded.

voyage.name: Deoksugung
voyage.price: Adults (19 to 64 years old): ₩1,000 (groups: ₩800), children (aged 7–18) and soldiers: ₩500 (groups: ₩400), children 6 and under, seniors 65 and over: free
voyage.content: Deoksu Palace vividly contrasts with the other nearby palaces like Changdeok Palace. Built during the mid-15th century, the architecture of the buildings inside are heavily influenced by Western designs. Hence, you will see a fusion of Korean and Western architecture. The stone-wall narrow way around the palace is a beautiful and famous path for the lovers, although there was a myth that they would break up when they

voyage.name: Namdaemun Gate
voyage.content: The Great South Gate is an iconic symbol of Seoul and has been designated as National Treasure Number 1. Particularly beautiful when floodlit at night, and best combined with a visit to the adjacent Namdaemun Market. Much of the structure was destroyed by arson in 2008, although a faithful reconstruction was completed in 2013. Formally known as 'Sungnyemun' (숭례문, 崇禮門). The other city gates can be found in the neighbo

voyage.name: Myeong-Dong Cathedral
voyage.content: Designed by a Coste priest, and build with financial support from the Paris Church Department, this was the house of Bum-Woo Kim and purchased by Marie Jean Gustave Blanc (under the Korean name Gamilro Kim). With a successful trade agreement in 1887, the cathedral was finally built in 1898. This building was the first church built with bricks. The height of the building proper is 23 m, but with the addition of the sp

voyage.name: T.um
voyage.content: The future of technology can often be seen today in South Korea, and SK Telecom have created a museum dedicated to it! Exhibits change frequently due to the rapid pace of technology being shown. Preschoolers not allowed. Online pre-registration necessary, make sure to reserve early as its gets full weeks in advance.

voyage.name: Seoul Museum of Art
voyage.content: Renovated from an old court building, it mainly exhibits contemporary art works. You can see installments and video arts as well as paintings and sculptures. A cafe is with a souvenir shop on the first floor.

voyage.name: Seoul City Hall
voyage.content: The old city hall was built under Japanese rule and it was renovated to a public library. In back of the old hall, the huge new city hall was built. In the basement, there is Citizen Hall, where musical performances and exhibitions are held for citizens. City Hall Square, in front of the hall, is open to public and political demonstrations. Every winter, Ice rink opens at the Square.

voyage.name: Culture Station Seoul 284
voyage.content: A culture center at the old Seoul Station. It was built in 1925 during the Japanese Colonial period, and the center of the Korean railway until 2004 when the current building for KTX opened. It reopened in 2011 as a culture center, and it hosts many exhibitions. The pre-modern architecture inspired by the Lucerene station (which has burnt down) offers unique sight among the glassy buildings of Seoul.

voyage.name: Seoullo 7017
voyage.content: A former motorway turned into pedestrian walkway. Opened in 2017, it offers a unique view above the cars and rails, with gardens and cafes along the path. Night view with car lights and neon signs is especially beautiful.

voyage.name: Seoul Anglican Cathedral
voyage.content: A central cathedral of the Diocese of Seoul. It was first built in 1920s and has a blended architecture of neo romanesque style with Korean traditional components.

voyage.name: Bank of Korea Money Museum
voyage.content: You can find out about 20,000 rare domestic and foreign currencies held by the Bank of Korea and the money manufacturing process and the country's economic process.

voyage.name: Korea Financial History Museum
voyage.content: It is a space where you can see Korea's financial development.

voyage.name: Stamp Museum
voyage.content: It is a space where you can see the process of mail change and various stamps of the world.

voyage.name: Rice Museum
voyage.content: It is a space where you can learn about the history of rice.

voyage.name: Agricultural Museum
voyage.content: It is a space where you can see various exhibitions on agriculture and traditional agricultural culture.

voyage.name: Seoul Animation Center
voyage.content: Seoul Animation Center (48, Sogong-ro, Jung-gu, Seoul, Republic of Korea) is a space where you can read over 30,000 comic books and animations for free, and is comprised of a 1st and 1.5-story duplex. Except for Mondays and other designated closed days, ‘Comics Cafe’ on the first floor is open from 10:00 to 20:00, and the admission fee is free. ‘Ani Picnic’ on the 2nd floor is open from 10:00 to 18:00, and the admiss

voyage.name: Seoul National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art Deoksu Palace
voyage.content: Various artworks are displayed differently from time to time. You have to pay an additional exhibition admission fee in addition to the entrance fee to Deoksugung Palace.

voyage.name: Seven Luck Casino
voyage.content: The casino is only accessible to foreigners (it is illegal for Korean citizens to gamble), so remember to bring your passport. Various card tables and slots are available to play. There is a bar and cafe that serve food and drinks, although expensive.

voyage.name: Sparex 24
voyage.price: Day arrival (5:00-20:00) ₩ 12,000 (child 7000), night arrival ₩ 15,000 (8000), out ticket ₩ 20,000. Food court meals ₩ 5000-30,000, drinks 3000-7000, snacks 2000-4000 including chips and instant noodles
voyage.address: 247 Jangchungdan-ro, Jung District, Seoul, Corée du Sud
voyage.content: This jjimjilbang or Korean sauna occupies two levels of mall basements. B3 is the entrance, big luggage store near reception, valuables storage at reception, shoes locker, separate showers and bath for men and women (with another larger locker, shared key with shoes locker, missing ventilation so if got wet clothes because of rain, let them out else won’t dry; bar soap) and an extra sleeping room per gender. B4 is th

voyage.name: Myeong-dong
voyage.content: Probably the best-known shopping area. It is definitely the most tourist-friendly fashion area. In spring and summer, fashion models/sidewalk promoters can be seen strolling the streets of Myeongdong promoting various cosmetics, stores or other fashion-related products. Many regular people also tend to catwalk their newest outfit on these streets. Rows of stores are available to look for that perfect accessory, and m

voyage.name: Namdaemun Market
voyage.content: The largest traditional street market in Korea. This market is in the center of Seoul and is a famous shopping place for tourists. Clothing for children and accessories are the most-commonly sold goods in this market, but there's lots of food as well and many outdoor eating options, especially in the evening. There is also a huge digital camera market in this area.

voyage.name: Hoehyeon Underground Shopping Center
voyage.content: Located within Myeong-dong, the Hoehyeon Underground Shopping Center contains the largest number of shops specializing in Korean and world numismatics for both local and international numismatists.

voyage.name: Lotte Young Plaza
voyage.content: *In renewal until Dec.31 2025* Just across the street from Avatar department store, this department store is oriented towards a younger, upscale clientele, and in addition to the usual Korean brands and international brands, the top floor of the space features an assortment of quality eating establishments to replenish your shopping energy. The wine bar is recommended. Sometimes art installations can be found on the

voyage.name: Migliore
voyage.content: One of the biggest fashion buildings in Seoul. It has 17 floors above ground and 7 basement floors. Information boards in Migliore are written in Korean as well as English, Japanese and Chinese for foreign tourists. US credit cards are often accepted, but ask before haggling if you aren't sure. The outside stage features a "talent show" of local dance groups (mostly high school or college student groups) most nights

voyage.name: Shinsegae
voyage.content: The oldest department store on the Korean peninsula. The original building was refurbished in 2008 and became a high-street boutique. Accepts major credit/debit cards, including Amex and JCB.

voyage.name: Gogung
voyage.content: Specialty restaurant for bibimbab at a moderate price.

voyage.name: Jeonju Jungang Hoegwan
voyage.content: This Korean restaurant specializes in the Jeonju variety of bibimbap, which features different ingredients and spices than other bibimbap dishes. Delicious and healthy.

voyage.name: Samarkand
voyage.content: In the heart of "Central Asian Town", which has Russian, Mongolian, Uzbek, and Central Asian restaurants. Wander around and discover the area a bit - you'll be rewarded with delicious food and an exotic experience.

voyage.name: Myeongdong Kyoja
voyage.content: Beef gyoza soup, unique dish but tasty.

voyage.name: Nampomyeonok
voyage.content: This is a restaurant specializing in cold buckwheat-based noodles (Pyongyang’s cold noodles). This is a place visited by former presidents such as Moon Jae-in, Lee Myung-bak and Yoon Seok-yeol. This restaurant is located in a lively narrow alley in an area dense with office buildings, and consists of a room with table-style seating and cushion-style tables.

voyage.name: Myeongdong Korean BBQ Mongvely
voyage.content: A popular all-you-can-eat Korean BBQ restaurant, offering unlimited premium pork and beef grilled over charcoal. With multilingual menus, a self-service buffet of fresh banchan, sauces, and a DIY ramen station, Mongvely combines local flavor with tourist-friendly service.

voyage.name: 82Olliienjeu
voyage.content: American-home-style restaurant with a cute interior.

voyage.name: Daeyeop Eulijoro Branch
voyage.content: Restaurant that specializes in Pyongyang naengmyeon and various Pyongyang food.

voyage.name: Yeonhaejang
voyage.content: It is a restaurant specializing in pork small intestine hot pot that features a clean and modern interior, and is loved by many customers even if the waiting is long. They have gopchang hot pot with a variety of side menus, and the soup of the hot pot boasts a deep and thick taste and uses fresh gopchang without any odor. In addition, it is sold as a meal kit, so you can enjoy it easily at home.

voyage.name: Gangsanok
voyage.content: Opened in 1958, the restaurant specializes in traditional soybean dishes that serve only soybean noodles in the summer and serve soybean meal for the rest of the year. It is open for only two and a half hours a day, and needs to be careful when visiting because it can be closed early when the ingredients are exhausted. It consists of thick and savory soybean soup and chewy noodles, and is served with kimchi.

voyage.name: Bakgane Bindaetteok Main Branch
voyage.address: jongrogu jongro32 street 7 gwangjang market 1st floor
voyage.content: It is the representative restaurant of Gwangjang Market, which has been around since 1966, and serves savory and crispy bindaetteok by grinding 100% green beans directly into a millstone. It is also popular with foreign tourists, has a variety of menus and friendly service.

voyage.name: Hanwoojeong
voyage.content: Korean BBQ restaurant specializing in 1++ Korean Hanwoo beef, Korea’s highest-quality beef grade. Inspired by the elegance of a traditional hanok, Hanwoojeong provides refined Korean dining and a warm, sophisticated atmosphere. Guests can experience carefully selected cuts including sirloin, striploin, tenderloin and other premium specialties, complemented by Korean side dishes and classic accompaniments.

voyage.name: RAndy's Bar
voyage.content: Foreign-owned bar in front of Hankook University of Foreign Studies known for a varied clientele, great pool table, and affordable prices. Has Red Rock and Hoegaarden on tap.

voyage.name: Mezz Bar
voyage.content: Bar known for cocktails

voyage.name: Levenbroee
voyage.content: Known for beer but also due to the view from the bar, which is amazing.

voyage.name: 2MOON Cafe & Pub
voyage.content: Low key, cozy cafe tucked away on the rooftop of a low building. Serves tea, coffee, drinks and cocktails. Quiet and very atmospheric at night, great for conversations, popular with and seemingly known only to locals. Owner speaks fluent English, studied in Texas and is happy to chat. Some of the clothing made downstairs by indie designers is sold here too.

voyage.name: Jaehaeseok
voyage.content: It is a pudding specialty cafe that boasts a unique vintage interior and cozy atomosphere.

voyage.name: Asoto Bakery
voyage.content: It is a bakery with a cute atmosphere where you can feel the Japanese Kitsaten sensibility.

voyage.name: Gonggangap
voyage.content: It is a dessert cafe located in Euljiro, especially famous for pudding bingsu and various cakes

voyage.name: Ling Ling
voyage.content: It is a space famous for its Y2K sensibility and kitschy interior. It offers a variety of desserts and drinks, and cakes and jelly sodas are especially popular. The interior of the store is cozy and has many photo zones, making it a great place to take pictures. Also, cute props and goods are on sale, so it entertains visitors.

voyage.name: Bekarong Bagel
voyage.content: A handmade bagel specialty store, all bagels are hand-rolled and feature a light, chewy texture. A takeout specialty store, it also offers a variety of cream cheese and bagel sandwiches, and it's affordable and cost-effective.

voyage.name: Able Hostel/Guesthouse
voyage.address: No. 205, Unit 1, Kumho twin tower, 89-1, Gwanghui-dong
voyage.content: New, comfortable, young clientele, with decent baths and a friendly owner and staff. Each room has computers available for free Internet use, Wi-Fi throughout. This place is near Dongdaemun Market but very quiet when you sleep. No curfew. Kitchen, free laundry.

voyage.name: IMI Hotel
voyage.content: At the higher end of the love hotel spectrum, some rooms feature Japanese spas and oxygen generators.

voyage.name: Namsan Guesthouse
voyage.content: In the shadow of Seoul Tower in Namsan Park. Free Internet access, free breakfast, kitchen.

voyage.name: Seoul Backpackers
voyage.content: Backpacker hangout with English-speaking staff. Free Internet. Laundry ₩5,000.

voyage.name: Silloam Sauna
voyage.content: This is a very large jjimjilbang with great facilities, but the family atmosphere of other jjimjilbangs is sometimes lacking. The locker-room staff will stow oversized luggage if you ask, and a morning wake-up call can be arranged. Sleeping facilities are excellent, clean, comfortable and usually fairly quiet. There are two large dormitories for men and women, plus a snorers' room which sounds like a dragon's lair. T

voyage.name: Zaza Backpackers
voyage.content: Helpful English speaking staff help you to feel right at home. Free Wi-Fi, 24 hr access, Private bathroom in each room. 24 hr security, towels and hairdryer for hire, parking. Tour info and booking service. Free international phone.

voyage.name: Seoul Municipal Youth Hostel
voyage.content: Once the epicentre of terror and torture of the Korean Central Intelligence Agency before democracy, its headquarters is now a government-run youth hostel that provides affordable accommodation. Young travellers under 24 are entitled to a discounted price. Outside the hostel there is also a basement used as a torture chamber, which is refurbished as a museum.

voyage.name: Ibis Hotel Myeongdong
voyage.content: Very central, free internet access.

voyage.name: Lotte Hotel
voyage.content: Grand old lady of downtown Seoul's hotels with 1,300 rooms, all kept in tip-top shape. The obvious choice for ornate Korean luxury.

voyage.name: Plaza Hotel
voyage.content: Completely redesigned as Korea’s luxury boutique hotel in 2010, The Plaza is now an exceptionally beautiful, independent luxury hotel in the heart of the business, shopping, and entertainment districts of Seoul.

voyage.name: Shilla Seoul
voyage.content: One of the city's premier hotels. It was built by the Park Chung-hee government in 1967 as the state guest house for visiting foreign dignitaries, and was converted to a luxury hotel in 1979. While the hotel guest rooms are in a modern 1970s high-rise building, the original state guest house, known as Yeong Bin Gwan and built in a traditional Korean architectural style, has been preserved on the hotel property and ca

voyage.name: Se-Jong
voyage.content: This hotel has the beautiful view including the Namsan Tower

voyage.name: Gwanghwamun Plaza
voyage.content: A center of Seoul. The name came from the main gate of the Gyeongbokgung. The site was a location of the Six Ministries during the Joseon dynasty and was a large motorway since then. In 2009, the middle of the road was opened to the public as a renovation project. It's now home to festivals and events. There are two statues in the plaza: Admiral Yi Sun-sin (a legendary admiral who won numerous important battles again

voyage.name: Gyeongbokgung
voyage.hours: Opens at 09:00, closes between 17:00 and 18:30 depending on the season, closed Tuesdays; last admission 1 hour before closing
voyage.content: This is Seoul's grandest Joseon Dynasty-era palace and the seat of power for centuries before it was razed in 1592 by a Japanese invasion (and again by the Japanese in 1910). This was the first palace used by the Joseon Dynasty and was constructed after King Taejo founded the Joseon Dynasty and moved the capital to Hanyang. Large parts have now been restored, and the vast grounds also house the Joseon Palace Museum a

voyage.name: Changdeokgung
voyage.content: Second only to Gyeongbokgung in historical importance, it was built in 1405 and was the seat of power between 1618 and 1896. The buildings have been restored to create a dazzling but still elegant effect that got the palace listed as a . The site is better preserved than Gyeongbokgung. Buildings of particular note include the blue-roofed Seonjeongjeon, which was the King's office, and the Daejojeon ("Great Making Hal

voyage.name: Changgyeonggung
voyage.content: It was built in 1104 as a summer palace for the Kings of the Goryeo Dynasty and became one of the main palaces during the Joseon Dynasty. The palace was used as a temporary home for the King during the time Gyeongbuk Palace was being built. Unlike other palaces that have a North-South orientation, Changgyeong Palace faces East-West. Also, this palace is known for connecting to Jongmyo Shrine, a holy place for the Jos

voyage.name: Gyeonghui-gung
voyage.content: It was built in the 17th century, and was burnt down twice in the 19th century. It was largely destroyed by the Japanese during colonial rule to build a school for Japanese children. It was finally restored in 1985 and opened to the public.

voyage.name: Unhyeongung
voyage.content: A museum in the former palace of a Joseon Dynasty archduke Heungseon, who was the father of the second last king of Joseon. It has several mannequins depicting the costumes of the yangban or noble class during the Joseon Dynasty. The palace buildings themselves represent the style of the Joseon noble class' mansion well.

voyage.name: Jongmyo Shrine
voyage.hours: Wed-Mon: Feb-May/Sep-Oct: 09:00-18:00; Jun-Aug: 09:00-18:30; Nov-Jan: 09:00-17:30; closed Tue
voyage.content: The royal ancestral temple during the Joseon Dynasty, this is where the kings would perform sacrificial rituals in honor of their ancestors. Certainly, the most famous shrine devoted to the royal family members of Korean dynasties. The grounds are a bit more walker-friendly than some of the palaces, admission is cheaper, and they also have some interactive equipment available to learn about the rituals and ceremonies

voyage.name: Jogyesa Temple
voyage.content: The chief temple of the Jogye order of Buddhism, the dominant branch of Buddhism in Korea. As such, it is one of the most important modern Buddhist temples in the country. That being said, Jogyesa Temple is rather small, and if time permits, Bongeunsa in Gangnam is a larger and more interesting Buddhist temple.

voyage.name: Dongdaemun Gate
voyage.content: More formally known as Heunginjimun (흥인지문, 興仁之門), the old eastern gate of the city still stands. Though not as impressive architecturally as Namdaemun, the Dongdaemun market is infinitely more interesting than its counterpart.

voyage.name: Sukjeongmun Gate
voyage.address: San 25-22, Samcheong-dong 서울 성북구 성북동 산 25-22

voyage.name: National Folk Museum Children's Museum
voyage.content: This place provides various experiences and services for children in areas such as exhibitions, education, research, and exchange.

voyage.name: Hyehwa Moon
voyage.content: It is located at the border between Seongbuk-gu and Jongno-gu, and it is related to Jongno-gu, so I inserted it in the Jongno-gu compartment.

voyage.name: Museum Kimchikan
voyage.content: A museum (previously known as Kimchi Field Museum) about all things kimchi. Includes a lot of interactive exhibits and comes with a free audio guide in English. There are also hands-on kimchi-making programs, only on reservation, however.

voyage.name: National Museum of Korean Contemporary History
voyage.content: Since its independence from Japan, Korea has experienced a series of political events during a short period. You can see exhibitions that show war, dictatorships, uprisings against dictatorships, and industrialization that happened in South Korea.

voyage.name: MMCA Seoul (National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Korea)
voyage.price: ₩4,000. Free for ages under 24 or over 65, college students, and on the last Wednesday of each month
voyage.hours: Mon Tue Thu Fri Sun 10:00-18:00; Wed Sat 10:00-21:00 (18:00-21:00: free), closed on January 1st, Lunar New Year’s Day, Korean Thanksgiving Day
voyage.content: MMCA is mainly located at the Gwacheon, near the Seoul Grand Park. MMCA Seoul opened in 2013. The site had been the Korean Armed Forces Capital Hospital and the Defense Security Command. MMCA Seoul has an art and culture complex equipped with exhibition and education buildings, a digital lab, a multi-project hall, and a theater. The building is unique and won Grand Prizes at the 2014 Korean Architecture Awards.

voyage.name: Seoul Museum of History
voyage.content: Seoul has been the capital of Korea since 1392, and this museum focuses on its history during Joseon Dynasty, the Japanese annexation period, and modern development.

voyage.name: Seoul Craft Museum
voyage.content: The Seoul Craft Museum can experience the technical, practical, artistic, and cultural values of crafts by studying and sharing not only crafts but also knowledge, records, people, and the environment surrounding crafts.

voyage.name: Seoul Museum of Education
voyage.content: The Seoul Education Museum opened on June 15, 1995, by displaying relics and photographs on educational systems, curriculum, educational contents, educational institutions, and educational activities to establish the status of Seoul education and present a bright future for future generations in the 21st century.

voyage.name: Beautiful Tea Museum
voyage.content: You can see artifacts or pottery related to tea here.

voyage.name: Police Museum
voyage.content: The Police Museum, which opened in 2005, is a space where you can preserve the history of the police and experience the activities of the police.

voyage.name: Hanyangdoseong Museum
voyage.content: Hanyangdoseong Museum is a museum that contains the history and culture of Hanyangdoseong from the Joseon Dynasty to the present. It is a cultural space with a permanent exhibition room, special exhibition room, data room, and study room.

voyage.name: Rice cake museum
voyage.content: You can see relics related to rice cake.

voyage.name: Seoul Our Sound Museum
voyage.content: A unique museum where you can see and hear traditional culture.

voyage.name: Newspaper Museum
voyage.price: Adult ₩4000, elementary school students~ university students ₩3000, free for older than 65 years old
voyage.content: The Newspaper Museum offers a panoramic view of the 130-year history of Korean newspapers since the first modern newspaper in Korea, Hanseong Sunbo (1883).

voyage.name: National Weather Museum
voyage.content: The National Weather Museum can see the development of modern weather technology from the history of weather observation to the current day world of supercomputers.

voyage.name: Bukchon Oriental Culture Museum
voyage.content: You can see various exhibitions of the museum, and there is an observatory where you can see Seoul City Wall and Gyeongbokgung Palace.

voyage.name: World Museum of Decorations
voyage.content: It is a space where you can learn the history, culture, society, and art of various ethnic groups through ornaments.

voyage.name: National Museum of Buddhism
voyage.content: This place works as a museum at the center of Korean Buddhism, it holds a meaningful special exhibition every year and can feel the traditional culture closer Prepare education.

voyage.name: PKM gallery
voyage.content: Established in 2001, PKM Gallery is known for its sleek, modern architecture and thoughtfully curated exhibitions that span painting, sculpture, multimedia, and installation art. The gallery actively participates in global art fairs and supports emerging and established artists alike, making it a significant player in South Korea's contemporary art scene. It offers visitors an immersive cultural experience, surrounde

voyage.name: Whanki Museum
voyage.content: The Whanki Museum, nestled in the serene hills of Buam-dong in Seoul, is dedicated to the life and work of renowned Korean abstract artist Kim Whanki. Opened in 1992, this museum showcases Kim's distinctive abstract works that blend traditional Korean themes with modern abstract forms, creating a unique visual language. The museum’s architecture harmonizes with its natural surroundings, offering visitors a peaceful e

voyage.name: National Children's Science Museum
voyage.content: It is a science museum for children.

voyage.name: Tapgol ("Pagoda") Park
voyage.content: A small park frequented by the elderly and the footsore traveler, just to the east of Jongmyo Shrine. Contains a 500-year-old namesake pagoda under protective glass and a nice large gazebo to get out of the sun. This is where the Korean constitution was first read aloud by the public during the 20th century. Acts as a navigation landmark when moving between Myeong-dong, Jong-no, and Insa-dong neighborhoods.

voyage.name: Cheong Wa Dae
voyage.content: Also known in English as the Blue House, it was the residence of the President of the Republic of Korea from 1948-2022. It's next to the grounds of Gyeongbokgung, and can be easily recognized by its blue roof tiles and its unique fusion of modern and traditional Korean architectural styles. It is now open to the public, but only allows a limited number of visitors per day, so be sure to reserve your tickets in advanc

voyage.name: Sungkyunkwan
voyage.content: Sungkyunkwan was the highest educational institution during the Joseon dynasty since 1398. Students, including the royal family, studied Confucianism and other courses in Sungkyunkwan and became government officials and scholars. Munmyo was a Confucian shrine in Sungkyunkwan, and a ceremonial rite called 'Seokjeon Daeje' is performed twice a year. The current Sungkyunkwan University is a modern successor of Sungkyunk

voyage.name: Cheonggyecheon
voyage.content: It is a trail where you can take a walk along the river. The stream is a popular recreational area with walking paths, small waterfalls, and over 20 bridges, providing a peaceful escape in the heart of the city. Cheonggyecheon is also illuminated at night, making it a scenic spot for visitors to enjoy both the natural and urban landscapes. It’s especially popular during seasonal festivals, like the Seoul Lantern Fest

voyage.name: Bukchon Observatory
voyage.content: Provides a sweeping view of Bukchon Village and the greater Seoul cityscape, with Lotte Tower and the palace both clearly visible. It’s humble: clearly a converted apartment, and so tucked away its easy to miss, but it’s a great place to rest and take in the views, with beverage (tea, coffee) included as part of admission.

voyage.name: Bukak palgakjung
voyage.content: You can see the night view of Seoul from the observation deck located on Mt. Bukak.

voyage.name: Hongik University Daehakro Art Center
voyage.address: 128-8 Hongik University Daehak-ro Art Center, Yeongeon-dong
voyage.content: It is a musical theater and cultural complex consisting of a large theater with 702 seats, a small theater with 150 seats, and two large exhibition rooms. It has the best facilities in the nearby Daehak-ro area.

voyage.name: Naksan Park
voyage.content: It is a park that runs from Dongdaemun to Hyehwa-dong. From the top of the park, you can see the night view of Seoul.

voyage.name: Bukchon Hanok Village
voyage.content: The collective name of the few tiny suburbs ("dong") wedged between Gyeongbuk Palace and the Secret Garden, just north of Insadong and Anguk Station. This area was where relatives of the royal family, high public officials, and other important families lived for over 500 years as they serviced the nearby palaces. Today, some 900 of their traditional Korean "hanok" houses remain, making this area one of Seoul's most p

voyage.name: Inwangsan Mountain
voyage.content: This 336-m hill is home to the eponymous Inwang Temple (Inwangsa) and to Seoul's most famous shamanist shrine Guksadang (국사당). To get there, take Exit 2 and start climbing uphill following the "Inwang Temple" signs, through the huge construction site, and up through the temple gate. You'll see a map board and several paths. Take the left staircase upward, past the bronze bell of Bongwonsa, and you'll reach Guksadang.

voyage.name: Hyehwa
voyage.alt: 혜화 – colloquially known as Daehangno (대학로, lit. university road)
voyage.content: Performing arts center. Many small theaters with live dramatic and comedic performances lining every street. This district is filled with life and street commerce past midnight. The name came after the Seoul National University, which was located here before it moved to Gwanak-gu. SNU Hospital and Seoul National University School of Medicine one of the best in the country, is still here.

voyage.name: Sejong Center for Performing Arts
voyage.content: Oldest and one of the largest multi-purpose theatres in downtown Seoul and home of Seoul Philharmonic. The biggest pipe organ in East Asia is in its Great Auditorium, and several video art pieces from Nam June Paik are in the entrance of the auditorium.

voyage.name: Institute of Korean Royal Cuisine
voyage.hours: For class times, inquire in advance
voyage.content: As the name implies, you learn how to prepare royal cuisine, as well as rice cakes and hangwa (Korean cookies).

voyage.name: O'ngo Food Communications
voyage.hours: For class times, inquire in advance
voyage.content: Learn to make authentic Korean dishes in English or Japanese from Korean chefs. O'ngo Food Communications offers classes to make bulgogi and kimchi, Korean barbecue, and Vegan Temple Cuisine. You get a tour of a traditional Korean Market after the classes to see Korean ingredients and people.

voyage.name: The lantern light festival
voyage.content: Every November, the lantern light festival takes place at Cheonggye Creek. At the festival, you can see many lanterns made by Korean and foreign artists. Some of the lanterns are in traditional Korean style, and there are also many character lanterns and company mascot lanterns.

voyage.name: Rent Korean Traditional Clothes
voyage.content: When you visit Gyeongbokgung (경복궁), Changdeokgung (창덕궁), or any palace near Jongno you can rent traditional Korean clothes and enter for a free visit. You will be able to embrace Korean culture and make great memories in Seoul. You can rent traditional Korean clothes for around ₩20,000, get a traditional Korean hairstyle for women and keep it for 2 hours.

voyage.name: Aruto Small Theater
voyage.content: Located in the Daehak-ro district, Aruto Small Theater is known for staging romantic comedies. Since 2023, the theater is showcasing the play "De-minus Back to Fall in Love," a lighthearted romantic comedy. This small venue offers a cozy setting for audiences to enjoy live theater in an informal atmosphere.

voyage.name: LOL Park
voyage.content: It is the place where League of Legends matches take place, and there are many PC rooms in the same building, so there are many things to enjoy

voyage.name: Dongdaemun Market
voyage.content: Though not as impressive architecturally as Namdaemun, the Dongdaemun market is infinitely more interesting than its counterpart.

voyage.name: Gwangjang Market
voyage.content: Famous traditional market in Seoul. It was one of the first permanent markets in Korea, and it is always crowded. It has a variety of silk, linen, and other traditional items. Street food is really excellent as well, especially bindaetteok(Mung Bean Pancakes).

voyage.name: Insadong
voyage.content: Insadong is an area known for its art galleries and shops and is possibly the most touristy place in South Korea. It is a great place to buy cultural souvenirs. There are also a few stores that offer interesting vintage toys and various kitsch. Insadong also contains many traditional tea and coffee shops. It is one of the few places where vegetarian restaurants can be found.

voyage.name: Ssamziegil
voyage.content: Ssamziegil is a shopping complex that opened in 2004. It has the form of a rectangular spiral on three floors and includes about a hundred craft shops (clothing, jewelry, leather, etc.), restaurants, and cafes, also make-your-own crafts like candles, pottery, etc.

voyage.name: The store from Tong-In
voyage.content: Occupying four floors, this store offers high-quality items, including pottery, inlaid, and lacquered objects, as well as jewelry, postcards, etc. Not necessarily cheap, but the quality is good. It is located a little further than Ssamziegil on the same side as Insadong-gil.

voyage.name: Kyobo Book Store
voyage.content: Kyobo is the largest chain of bookstores in South Korea, and this flagship store is located in the center of Seoul. It is completely invisible from the outside because it is underground. It is accessed directly from the Gwanghwamun subway station or at the intersection of Sejongno and Jongno. There is a huge selection of books, CDs, DVDs, stationery items, cardmaking, and a bunch of other accessories (there are even

voyage.name: Imun Seolnongtang
voyage.content: The oldest extant restaurant in South Korea, founded around 1904. Serves seolleongtang (beef stew).

voyage.name: Sadongmyenok
voyage.content: Justly famous for its manduguk, a soup of gargantuan homemade dumplings stuffed with meat and veggies and served with side dishes for ₩5,000. English menu available.

voyage.name: Gung
voyage.content: Specialty restaurant for mandu (Korean dumplings) from the nearby Kaesong region in North Korea. The chickpea patties are also very good. This restaurant has been passed down from mother to daughter for three generations.

voyage.name: Everest
voyage.content: Nepali restaurant featuring dozens of delectable dishes ranging from mutton curry to butter naan. Bollywood music videos are free.

voyage.name: Samcheong Sujaebi
voyage.content: Canteen style ambiance, renowned for serving good Sujaebi - a mild soup where the noodles are flattened and torn into sheets. Always packed with people so be prepared for a queue.

voyage.name: Tosokchon
voyage.content: Reverently referenced in most local guides as the place for Ginseng chicken soup and variations on that theme.

voyage.name: Hakrim Dabang
voyage.content: Opened in 1956, this is the oldest extant coffee shop (in Korean, 다방; dabang) in Seoul. Known for its vintage charm, cozy wooden interiors, and retro vibe, Hakrim Dabang offers a nostalgic experience reminiscent of the old Seoul. It’s particularly famous for its hand-drip coffee, tea, and classic menu items like the "Vienna coffee," served with a generous topping of whipped cream. The café is a beloved spot for artis

voyage.name: Jung Don
voyage.content: This restaurant serves Japanese-style pork cutlets. It's so popular that it's been featured on a popular Korean food program.

voyage.name: Local Village(토속촌)
voyage.content: It sells samgyetang, a traditional Korean dish, and ginseng liquor.

voyage.name: Pitzeriao
voyage.content: This is the place to go for wood-fired pizza. They serve pasta and pizza, so if you're looking for a western restaurant, this is the place to go.

voyage.name: Yukhoe Sisterhood(육회자매집)
voyage.content: In Korea, lean cuts of beef with less fat are cut into small pieces, seasoned, and eaten as sashimi. It tastes great when paired with the fruit pear and egg yolk. However, be careful when eating sashimi with octopus, also known 'San Naggi (산낙지)', as it can be offensive. Of course, the octopus is trimmed after it dies, but its nerves are still alive and it can wiggle.

voyage.name: Manson Hoff
voyage.content: It's known for its cold draft beer, nogari, and chicken. It's especially popular in the fall when the weather is nice and in the summer when it's hot.

voyage.name: Tteoksang
voyage.content: This restaurant offers a fusion of Korean tteokbokki (rice cakes) in a hanok charming setting.

voyage.name: Pungnyeon Ssal Nongsan
voyage.content: cheap snack places. noodle sausage, fried stuff, fried rice cake...

voyage.name: Jin A Chun
voyage.content: The second oldest operating restaurant in Seoul, having been founded in 1925. Serves Korean Chinese cuisine.

voyage.name: Yukmian
voyage.content: Yukmian is a restaurant that offers beef noodle dishes, located near Daehak-ro. The menu features various cuts of beef served with noodles in a broth. The restaurant is known for its focus on quality ingredients and simple preparation. Due to its popularity, reservations may be required during busy hours.

voyage.name: a buckwheat-flavored restaurant
voyage.content: This restaurant specializes in dishes made from buckwheat, offering a variety of traditional Korean meals. Located in the Daehak-ro area, it provides a menu that highlights buckwheat as a key ingredient, including noodles and pancakes. The simple setting and focus on buckwheat-based dishes attract those seeking a unique dining experience.

voyage.name: UjauKimchi Tteokbokki
voyage.content: Yuja Yoo Tteokbokki is a restaurant that specializes in tteokbokki, a popular Korean dish made from rice cakes. The restaurant offers a variety of tteokbokki options with different levels of spice and flavors.

voyage.name: Hyehwa Dodam
voyage.content: It is a famous restaurant for Korean traditional foods such as kimchi stew and pajeon. They also sell Korean traditional makgeolli.

voyage.name: Hyehwa Gopchang
voyage.content: It is a restaurant where you can eat assorted tripe at a low price.

voyage.name: Uyeonhwa
voyage.content: The Hanok-style restaurant in Ikseon-dong blends modern sensibilities and traditional atmosphere. It features Hamburg steak made with 100 percent Korean beef and is served with hot pot rice.

voyage.name: Ikseon-dong Meat Restaurant
voyage.price: ₩18,000 per 180 g serving, pork set for two ₩54,000
voyage.content: Korean barbecue in a hanok with exposed wooden rafters, where staff grill the meat at your table. Korean pork cuts such as minari samgyeopsal, galmaegisal and kkotmoksal, plus wagyu sirloin and kimchi jjigae. Group seating and outdoor tables in the alley.

voyage.name: Sinrajemyeon Anguk Branch
voyage.content: It is a kalguksu specialty store that originated in Gyeongju, and is located in Anguk Station in Seoul. It features a traditional Korean interior with a luxurious atmosphere.

voyage.name: Chwiyabeolguksi
voyage.content: Dumpling hot pot is a particularly famous noodle restaurant. Dumpling hot pot here boasts a deep and cool taste of soup with a combination of large dumplings and fresh vegetables.

voyage.name: Eomyongbaek pork soup
voyage.content: It is a restaurant that serves Busan style pork and rice soup in a tranquil hanok atmosphere. The main menu here is pork and rice soup in two styles, clear and thick, and kimchi and kkakdugi, served as basic side dishes, go well with gukbap.

voyage.name: GwanghwamunMijin
voyage.content: As a traditional buckwheat specialty, cold buckwheat noodles and handmade pork cutlet are the main dishes. The restaurant is spacious and quick-rotating, and the Yeolmu Kimchi and pickled radish served as standard side dishes are delicious.

voyage.name: Dooly snack
voyage.content: It is a restaurant that sells snacks in Hyehwa-dong. It sells a variety of menus at low prices. You can only pay in cash.

voyage.name: Queensgard
voyage.content: The British pub. Introducing a range of lesser-known British drinks and foods, including infused gins, a variety of London dry gins, British beers, and ciders.

voyage.name: CHILLIN
voyage.content: An atmospheric cafe and bar on University Road.

voyage.name: AcefourClub
voyage.content: A coffee and liquor store in a converted tea room.

voyage.name: Sunset Records
voyage.content: It's a place that accepts submissions and enjoys singing and drinking.

voyage.name: Friends
voyage.content: It's a multinational, multicultural bar that doesn't care about race, gender identity, or anything else.

voyage.name: Goen
voyage.content: Goen in Hyehwa is a Japanese restaurant that offers a variety of dishes, including sushi, sashimi, and other traditional Japanese cuisine. The restaurant is known for its fresh ingredients and authentic flavors, providing a comfortable dining experience in a casual setting.

voyage.name: Beonteu Seoul
voyage.content: Located between Cheonggyecheon and Jongno, it is a three-story large bakery cafe that features a large space and a variety of bakery menus. In particular, it offers a leisurely atmosphere where people can share coffee and bread while enjoying the view of Cheonggyecheon.

voyage.name: Artist Bakery
voyage.content: It is a bakery specializing in various kinds of salt bread, featuring a savory and salty taste.

voyage.name: Coffee one
voyage.content: Located in Gwanghwamun, it is famous for its fat sandwiches and various puddings.

voyage.name: SioPangya Gwanghwamun D Tower Branch
voyage.content: Based on authentic Japanese salt bread recipes, it is a takeout specialty store that provides rich salt bread using French gome butter.

voyage.name: Sseolgeuregori Stroop waffle
voyage.content: This cafe specializes in Stroop waffle, an authentic Dutch dessert, and serves fresh waffles that are made on the fly.

voyage.name: Hotel Bricks
voyage.content: It's a quiet hotel. It provides free luggage storage and free Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: Bong House
voyage.content: Laid-back friendly guesthouse with Internet, Wi-Fi, purifier, washing machine, air-con, refrigerator, cable TV, gas oven, microwave oven, hair dryer, iron with ironing board and dryer for a fee of ₩5,000. The Bong bar which is right next to the Bong house. With each night stay you can claim 1 free beer from the bar.

voyage.name: Hostel Korea
voyage.content: Friendly English/Chinese-speaking staff. Free breakfast, free Wi-Fi, free laundry, air-con, hot water.

voyage.name: Seoul Guest House
voyage.content: Basic rooms with air-con in a traditional Korean-style house. Shared bathrooms, free Wi-Fi, and TV. For a higher price you can purchase a room with a private bath, television and computer with Internet. Some find it spartan, other like its homey feel, friendly owner and big, fluffy guard dog.

voyage.name: Wind Road & Flower Guesthouse
voyage.content: Free internet, laundry also available (but not free). The friendly staff speaks good English.

voyage.name: Yim's House
voyage.content: This excellent value hotel is unsure whether it caters to businessmen or backpackers. Rooms are clean and spacious, and Mr. Yim speaks fluent English.

voyage.name: Golden Pond Guesthouse
voyage.content: Comfortable, young atmosphere, with decent bathrooms and a friendly owner and staff. Two computers available for free Internet use, Wi-Fi throughout. This place is near a lot of pubs and restaurants, but very quiet when you sleep. No curfew. All staff is ready to hang out with guests every night. Sometimes they serve Korean meals for free. Kitchen, free laundry.

voyage.name: Hotel Artrium Jongno
voyage.content: There are free Wi-Fi and breakfast services. English and Japanese are available.

voyage.name: Seodaemun Prison
voyage.content: The prison was built in 1908, and became infamous during the Japanese occupation when it was used to torture, starve and execute Korean political prisoners. Actual prison cells, wax figures and videos are used to demonstrate the shocking brutality experienced there. Most signs are in Korean although volunteer guides can describe the sights in English. The content may not be suitable for those of a sensitive nature.

voyage.name: World Cup Stadium
voyage.content: It was South Korea's main stadium in the 2002 World Cup and is home to FC Seoul.

voyage.name: Seodaemun Museum of Natural History
voyage.content: At this museum you can learn more about geology, archeology and biology. Plenty of fossils on display, interactive exhibitions and various activities for kids.

voyage.name: Worldcup Park
voyage.content: Worldcup Park has several sections. Sky Park is the most popular for the Silver Grass Festival. The park used to be a waste landfill.

voyage.name: Trickeye Museum
voyage.content: Trickeye Museum features optical illusion paintings and installations. Divided into six themed galleries, visitors can freely touch, step inside 3D exhibits and take photos.

voyage.name: Castle Praha
voyage.content: A Czech brewery and restaurant, with outside facade being a replica of Prague's Astronomical clock.

voyage.name: Korean Film Museum
voyage.hours: 10:30-18:30 (10:30~17:30 on Sat and Sun, Closed on Mon)
voyage.address: 400 World Cup Buk-ro, Mapo-gu, 1st floor of the Korea Film Archive
voyage.content: The Korean Film Museum is divided into a permanent exhibition and temporary exhibitions. The permanent exhibition introduces the history of Korean films in chronological order and operates an experience zone. The exhibitions are held under various themes so that you can watch and enjoy Korean movies from a new perspective.

voyage.name: The Hyundai Seoul
voyage.content: A Hyundai Department Store brand, it's home to all things fashion, hip-hop, food, and dessert.

voyage.name: Nanji Hangang Park
voyage.content: Nanji Hangang Park is one of South Korea's famous Han River parks, known for its water features, fountains, festivals, and camping.

voyage.name: Mang-Won Hangang Park
voyage.content: Seoul's first Hamsang Theme Park, Hangang Park is famous for its water-based leisure activities.

voyage.name: Yeouido Hangang Park
voyage.content: Yeouido Hangang Park is famous for being the site of the World Fireworks Festival, held every October.

voyage.name: Hongdae Playground
voyage.content: The area around here in Hongik University is completely packed with shops and restaurants aimed solely at University students. Definitely an interesting way to spend some hours exploring the streets and see how Korean students let their hair down. Dinner can be had in this area at student prices, or avail yourself to one of the many street stalls serving Korean student street food.

voyage.name: Hongjecheon Stream
voyage.content: Hongjecheon Stream is an urban stream in Seoul, South Korea, flowing through the districts of Seodaemun-gu and Mapo-gu. It provides a recreational space for residents with walking paths, greenery, and scenic views along its banks.

voyage.name: Ewha Women's University Market
voyage.content: At the front gate of Ewha Women's University, visitors can find a dense market geared towards young women. You can find stores that sell clothes, shoes, hats, handbags, and so on. There are also clothes for men, and franchise stores. The campus itself is beautiful.

voyage.name: Kakao Friends Hongdae Flagship Store
voyage.content: A merchandise store for mascots of the omnipresent KakaoTalk messenger app. Very cute Character designs.

voyage.name: MINISO Hongdae
voyage.content: A variety store near Hongik University Station selling stationery, household goods, accessories, cosmetics and character merchandise.

voyage.name: Cowoozy
voyage.content: A vintage clothing shop in Hongdae selling secondhand and vintage fashion items.

voyage.name: Oticoti
voyage.content: A vintage clothing shop in Yeonnam-dong selling a selection of secondhand clothing and accessories.

voyage.name: Chagawoon Sweater
voyage.content: A vintage clothing shop in Yeonnam-dong selling secondhand clothing and accessories.

voyage.name: iomal
voyage.content: Focuses on a variety of pasta dishes, brunch plates, and beverage options rather than bakery or dessert items.

voyage.name: Hyang music (향뮤직)
voyage.content: Mostly CDs. All genres.

voyage.name: Purple records (메타복스)
voyage.content: Newly issued vinyls, CDs. Pop and Indies.

voyage.name: Metavox (메타복스)
voyage.content: Mostly second hand. CDs are main. Vinyl records covers also exist.

voyage.name: Gimbab records (김밥레코드)
voyage.content: A vintage clothing shop in Hongdae selling secondhand and vintage fashion items.

voyage.name: Jamdubong the 9
voyage.content: Korean pork belly with river views. It is located on a dock floating on the river.

voyage.name: Sosinitsso (소신이쏘)
voyage.content: This fusion galbi restaurant serves spicy Korean short ribs with cheese.

voyage.name: DamSan (담산)
voyage.content: This is the place to go for loin ribs, Korean gondre namulbap, and kimchi jeon.

voyage.name: GoSamE (고삼이)
voyage.content: This local restaurant serves Korean-style grilled fish and stir-fried squid.

voyage.name: GonangZi (고냉지)
voyage.content: The restaurant's signature dishes are bibimbap and kimchi stew.

voyage.name: HanLimDonGa (한림돈가)
voyage.content: This is the place to go for samgyeopsal, a Korean-style barbecue.

voyage.name: Miga
voyage.price: ₩ 8000-45000, Jeyuk Ssambap ₩20,000 for 2 or more persons (₩12,000 if single person), Osam Bulgogi ₩26,000 for 2 or more (₩15,000 if alone)

voyage.name: okmyeonga
voyage.content: chicken-specialized small restaurant with different types of noodles.

voyage.name: Grain Seoul
voyage.content: Build-your-own brunches and all-day mains in a thoughtful open space. English spoken.

voyage.name: Shin Migyeong Hongdae Dakgalbi
voyage.content: Great dakgalbi place just off the main night market street. Simple menu, cook it at your table. Good value and big portions!

voyage.name: jinjin
voyage.content: Jinjin is a Chinese restaurant in Seoul's Mapo-gu, offering a focused menu of about 10 dishes, known for its quality and traditional flavors. It has received the Michelin Bib Gourmand award for its good value. Signature dishes include Menbosha (shrimp toast) and stir-fried crab with egg white.

voyage.name: spaccanapoli
voyage.content: Known for authentic Neapolitan-style wood-fired pizza, this restaurant is highly praised for its use of traditional methods, including a real wood-fired oven. Popular menu items include the Margherita and Gorgonzola pizzas, and the ambiance is often described as vibrant and lively.

voyage.name: Uwa
voyage.content: Located in the bustling Hongdae area, Uwa offers a modern dining experience with a focus on casual yet trendy dishes. It is often visited for its eclectic menu and relaxed atmosphere, making it a go-to spot for younger crowds and students.

voyage.name: Hongdae SsiBooOng
voyage.content: A cozy café known for its desserts and drinks, this spot is famous for its photogenic ambiance. It’s a popular location for both locals and tourists looking for a quiet spot to relax in the busy Hongdae district.

voyage.name: yakitorimook
voyage.content: The restaurant handles fresh native chicken every day, grills it with the finest splints, and serves customers immediately

voyage.name: Analog Garden
voyage.content: Brunch menu has just one item: omelette-on-toast, but can be customized with add-ons. Rather popular with foreigners, service can be a bit chaotic but food is worth it. About 17000₩ for brunch with coffee.

voyage.name: Nambuk Tongil
voyage.content: A long-running Korean restaurant specializing in North Korean-style mandu. Popular dishes include mandu hot pot, dumpling soup, chicken kalguksu and mung bean pancakes.

voyage.name: lodge 190
voyage.content: Lodge 190 is a cozy café located along the Hongjecheon Stream in Seodaemun-gu, Seoul. Known for its signature French toast made with baguette and topped with seasonal fruits, the café offers a relaxing ambiance with views of Hongjecheon. The menu includes a variety of desserts, such as matcha shaved ice and yogurt bowls. Lodge 190 is also pet-friendly.

voyage.name: Beer O'Clock
voyage.content: This Canadian-run bar serves great pizzas and other grub in addition to showing sports on the big screen and offering darts. Weekends are pretty wild at this joint.

voyage.name: Woodstock
voyage.content: Around since 1991, the bar has prompted a slew of copycats but is the best place to hear classic rock and pop. The sound system is awesome and the owner/DJ knows his stuff. Expect large crowds Friday and Saturday nights and seeing people dance next to their tables. Great place to mix with Koreans of all ages.

voyage.name: Piehole
voyage.content: Piehole is a dessert café located in Sinchon, Seoul, specializing in a variety of homemade sweet pies and tarts. The interior features a cozy and vintage atmosphere with distinct, home-style decorative touches throughout the seating areas. It operates daily in the Sinchon commercial district, serving as a well-known local spot for dessert and coffee.

voyage.name: A slice
voyage.content: A Slice Cafe offers a selection of coffee, specialty drinks, and freshly baked pastries in a quiet, cozy atmosphere. The space is widely favored by students and locals looking for a comfortable spot to study or relax.

voyage.name: Miroir
voyage.content: Psychedelic hippie hangout with psytrance F and Sa, 1960s and 70s rock during the week.

voyage.name: 17°C
voyage.content: Located in Hongdae, chocolate bingsu and dark chocolate drinks are especially popular, making it an attractive space to serve a variety of chocolate drinks and desserts. The inside of the store is cozy and neat.

voyage.name: Before Blooming
voyage.content: It is a cake specialty cafe that offers a variety of cakes using seasonal fruits. Especially, fig cakes are popular, and the store provides a cozy and clean atmosphere to communicate with. It features a convenient ordering system through a kiosk and friendly service. In addition, it is known as a place for special days with the availability of holecakes.

voyage.name: Cafe Gongmyeong Yeonnam Branch
voyage.address: mapogu yeonhuiro 11 Korea Patent and Technology Promotion Agency Building 1st floor
voyage.content: It is a large cafe that offers top-class coffee and fresh baked bakery with cozy interior design. This is a space where customers can enjoy a variety of desserts, with ample seats and cozy lighting to help them relax. In particular, the signature drink 'Rise Latte' and the signature dessert 'Biscuit Shoe' are receiving positive reviews from many visitors. Also, various books are available throughout the cafe.

voyage.name: Sweet Hz
voyage.content: This cafe offers a variety of matcha and hojicha drinks and desserts with its cute interior and Japanese sensibility. In particular, matcha basque cheesecake and whipped cream cake are popular, and the dessert is not sweet and features the original taste of the ingredients. The interior of the cafe is decorated with warm lights and cute props, providing a comfortable atmosphere.

voyage.name: Mandongjegwa
voyage.content: Located in Yeonnam-dong, this takeaway specialty store offers a wide variety of bread. The interior of the store is compact, neat, and full of savory bread. The staff kindly provides tasting bread to help customers choose. Specifically, garlic baguette is a signature menu, featuring a rich garlic sauce and a soft texture. There is a wide variety of menus, and reservations are also available for convenience.

voyage.name: Orangji
voyage.content: It is a cafe famous for its cute interior design and cute desserts. Serving various matcha drinks and desserts, heart pancakes and kitty matcha tiramisu are especially popular. The inside of the cafe is white-toned and cozy, with props everywhere, making it a great place to take pictures. It is a place to enjoy dessert with friendly service.

voyage.name: Joaendoseun
voyage.content: It is a cafe famous for French toast and milk tea. It is decorated with a cozy and emotional interior, and customers appreciate the moist texture and unique taste of French toast. In particular, the combination of Maldon salt and maple syrup is impressive as French toast has a crispy outside and soft inside.

voyage.name: Peullemmeu
voyage.content: Located in Yeonnam-dong, the cafe offers a variety of desserts, such as souffle pancakes and croffles. This cafe has a cozy and quiet atmosphere, and it has various amenities for customers to spend their time comfortably. Souffles are cooked on the spot and take about 20-30 minutes. Specifically, souffle pancakes feature a soft and fluffy texture.

voyage.name: Turn down service
voyage.content: It's a quiet Woody emotional cafe, where LP music plays. Inside, it's compact and spacious, and offers a variety of handmade tarts and coffee menus. Specifically, the signature menu, Kernel Latte, boasts a savory and sweet taste with homemade nut creams on it. There is a two-hour limit.

Located in Yeonnam-dong, the cafe offers a variety of desserts according to the four seasons and boasts a cozy and warm atmosphere. It is decorated with an emotional interior, and the menu changes from season to season, and desserts using figs and corn are especially popular. Beverages and desserts are being evaluated for their excellent visuals and taste.

voyage.name: Maybe Cake
voyage.content: It is famous for whipped cream cakes that use fresh strawberries, and it is operated by reservation, so advance reservations are required. The cake is made with 100 percent animal whipped cream, which boasts a moderately sweet taste without being greasy. Also, the interior is decorated with a cute and pretty atmosphere.

voyage.name: Think Fruit
voyage.content: It is a cafe that specializes in souffles and various fruit desserts in Hongdae. The inside is neatly decorated in white tone, and it boasts a bright atmosphere with full glass. Souffles are made right on order and of high quality using Hagen-Dazs ice cream. It is especially popular with customers as it offers a wide variety of menus using seasonal fruits.

voyage.name: Rahel's kitchen Hongik Univ. Branch
voyage.content: It is a cafe that offers soft souffles and a variety of brunch menus. Inside, it is decorated with cute white and pink-toned interiors, and it is a space that feels open through the window. There are many kinds of souffles, and they are handmade and have a fresh taste. In addition, they can be accompanied by pets and come with chairs for infants.

voyage.name: Cafe Jang Ssam
voyage.content: Located in Hongik University, this cozy dessert cafe serves a wide variety of dacquoise and cakes. Specifically, dacquoise is loved by many visitors for its fluffy texture and the combination of chewy cream, and the price is also reasonable. The interior is decorated with warm wood-tone interiors.

voyage.name: Kitchen 205
voyage.content: It is a place that provides desserts produced and sold on the same day using fresh strawberries throughout the four seasons. Strawberry cakes here are especially loved for their freshness and quality. The store has a clean and cozy atmosphere.

voyage.name: Thrive Hongik Univ. Branch
voyage.content: It is a cafe famous for its unique interior design and various souffle menus that contain Jeju's sensibility. In particular, souffle is loved by many visitors for its soft and fluffy texture, and it is an attractive space to enjoy with various drinks.

voyage.name: Just Danbi
voyage.content: It's a real-time live place to deliver freshly baked crepes as soon as you order.

voyage.name: Judimari Hongik Univ. Branch
voyage.content: It is a dessert cafe famous for its cute interior and various pudding menus. In particular, the soft texture and rich taste of the pudding are loved by many visitors. The interior of the store is decorated with cute props, making it a great place to take pictures.

voyage.name: Cafe Letter
voyage.content: It is a bakery cafe that boasts a warm sensibility and cozy atmosphere, offering various kinds of bakery and specialty coffee. Especially, strawberry vanilla bun and croissant sandwiches are recommended as signature menus, and the cozy interior and meticulous service provide a comfortable experience for visitors.

voyage.name: Pioni Hongik Univ. Branch
voyage.content: A cake specialty store that has been in operation since 2008, it is famous for its fresh strawberry cream cake made using 100 percent animal whipped cream and fresh strawberries. The interior of the store is cozy and clean, and it is a popular destination for many customers as it offers a variety of drinks and cakes. In particular, cakes that are carefully made with all ingredients boast reliable and edible quality.

voyage.name: Kokorokara
voyage.content: A dessert shop in Yeonnam-dong specializing in handmade desserts and baked goods.

voyage.name: Pig Company Hongdae Korean BBQ
voyage.content: Pig Company is a pork-focused Korean BBQ spot in Myeongdong, known for cauldron lid grilling and crispy Korean fried chicken made fresh in-house. Built for sharing at the table.

voyage.name: Bangrang Hostel
voyage.content: 1 min from subway station, 2 min from airport bus stop.

voyage.name: Hongdae Guesthouse
voyage.content: Clean, spacious rooms with high ceilings, ondol heating, aircon, hot water. English spoken.

voyage.name: Seoul Walker Guesthouse
voyage.content: The owner, Mr. Yoo, speaks Korean, Japanese, and English. He is very friendly and always asks where you will go (in the morning) and where you went (at night). Laundry service is available for ₩5,000/cycle, which he will operate. He offers taxi service to and from Gimpo and Incheon airports, for ₩30,000 and ₩60,000, respectively. He has many pamphlets in different languages, books, a computer and printer, and WiFi. K

voyage.name: The Win Boutique Hotel
voyage.content: The basement dorm has a large common area and several bathrooms. Everything is clean, and access is 24-hr. Staff presence is minimal; reservations are recommended.

voyage.name: Best Western Premier Seoul Garden Hotel
voyage.content: Formerly the Holiday Inn, located in the Mapo area across from Yeouido Island.

voyage.name: Chocolate Tree
voyage.content: 109-91 Nogosan-dong, Mapo-gu (4 min from Line 2 Sinchon stn exit 7). Friendly and adorable English- and Chinese-speaking staff, free breakfast (toast, jam, peanut butter, eggs, coffee and tea), free wifi, free international phone call, free laundry, dryer, A/C, hot water, rooftop terrace, common area with kitchen. All rooms are equipped with desktop computer, refrigerator, big flat TV with cable TV on the wall. you c

voyage.name: Namsan Park
voyage.content: Namsan Park is a large park located in central Seoul, surrounding Namsan Mountain. Visitors can walk along the park's trails, enjoy views of the city, and observe plants and wildlife. The park is a popular place for walking and outdoor activities.

voyage.name: The National Museum of Korea
voyage.hours: Closed Mon; Tue Thu Fri 10:00-18:00; Wed Sat 10:00-21:00; Sun and holidays 09:00-19:00
voyage.content: Houses the best of the best collection of artifacts and relics from across Korea throughout different periods and dynasty. Also has some West Asian pieces from the Japanese Governor-General of Korea. Important exhibitions are Pensive Bodhisattva (bronze-Buddha statue from early 7th century), Goryeo Celadon Openwork Burner, Ten-Story Pagoda from Gyeongcheonsa Temple, and Gold Crown from Silla.

voyage.name: National War Memorial
voyage.content: A museum about Korean military history and the Korean War. It starts with the ancient and Middle Ages, explaining the wars at that time and showing the weaponry of the time. Then the second-floor deals with the Korean War, both focusing on the Korean and UN forces. Outside of the memorial, there are several fighter, bomber, and trainer aircraft displayed that were used during the Korean War.

voyage.name: N Seoul Tower
voyage.content: Once the tallest tower in Asia, it has the best panoramic view in all of Seoul. Many locals and visitors have visited the tower to catch a glimpse of the city’s landscape while enjoying the nature of Namsan Mountain and a host of other attractive facilities. Owing to the tower's unique structure, the observatory section boasts spectacular views of the changing foliage throughout all seasons. The tower can be reached

voyage.name: National Hangul Museum
voyage.content: With a big permanent exhibition hall divided in three: The Creation of Hangeul, Before the Invention of Hangeul, The principle behind the creation of Hangeul; and a small one for the special temporary topics (relating to Hangeul and other linguistic characters of the world), this place is a must-see to understand why the Koreans are so proud about their language.

voyage.name: Yongsan Museum of History
voyage.content: It is a museum where you can see the history of Yongsan, and there is a garden on the third floor.

voyage.name: Museum of Colonial History
voyage.content: It is the first history museum specializing in Japanese colonial era.

voyage.name: Kim Gu Memorial Hall
voyage.content: It is a memorial hall left to remember and record the history left by Kim Gu.

voyage.name: Namsan Outdoor Botanical Garden
voyage.content: You can see various trees and plants, and there is a way to take a walk.

voyage.name: Democracy and Human Rights Memorial Hall
voyage.alt: Formerly Namyeong-dong Anti-communist Branch 남영동 대공분실 (민주인권기념관)
voyage.content: History buffs may heard of the notorious "Seobinggo hotel" used by Chun Doo-hwan's Defense Security Command, but dissidents were more likely to be sent to anti-communist branches like Namyeong-dong before South Korea became a democracy. The branch, which functioned as an interrogation and torture chamber, was built in 1977. This is where university student Bak Jong-cheol was tortured to death, which led to massive pr

voyage.name: IPARKMALL Yongsan
voyage.content: A complex commercial facility that includes a shopping mall, convenience facilities, and stores. It consists of a building with 3 floors underground and 9 floors above ground. It is divided into The Center, Taste Park, Living Park, and Fashion Park, and has various stores including E Mart, LOTTE HIMART, CGV, and Young Poong Bookstore.

voyage.name: Leeum Museum of Art
voyage.content: The Leeum Museum of Art, located in Yongsan, Seoul, is a renowned museum showcasing both traditional Korean art and contemporary works, offering a unique cultural experience for visitors.

voyage.name: Yongsan Children's Garden
voyage.content: Yongsan Children's Garden is a public park located on the former site of a United States military base. The park features green spaces, walking paths, and recreational areas, offering visitors a place to relax and enjoy the outdoors. It also provides an opportunity to learn about the history of the former military base.

voyage.name: The Spa Grand Hyatt Seoul
voyage.content: The spa features a variety of massage treatments including a Korean massage, aromatherapy, and aroma stone treatment.

voyage.name: Great Korean Beer Festival
voyage.content: The Great Korean Beer Festival is held annually at the Younsan station: I-Park Mall.

voyage.name: Yongsan Electronics Market
voyage.content: Yongsan Station is in IMall which is another huge shopping mall with two storeys full of electronics. Without negotiating you can have cheaper prices than amazon.com. Yongsan is one option in Seoul if you are looking for electronics goods. Made up of over 20 buildings housing 5,000 stores, you can find appliances, stereos, computers and peripherals, office equipment, telephones, lighting equipment, electronic games a

voyage.name: Itaewon Foreign Bookstore
voyage.content: Probably the best place for English-language books, new or used, in Korea.

voyage.name: Dinermate Yongsan Branch
voyage.content: It is a dining bar where you can enjoy brunch cafes during the day and wine and bourbon in the evening. It is also a good place for dates and gatherings, as you can enjoy carefully prepared brunch menus, desserts, and various alcoholic beverages together in a modern and comfortable atmosphere.

voyage.name: Ueno
voyage.content: This is a Japanese home-style restaurant, and it is a place that contains a simple but deep taste and warmth like a hidden restaurant in a small alley in Japan.

voyage.name: Siok
voyage.content: Shiok is a Singaporean restaurant that reproduces the local taste of Singapore, meaning "delicious" and "cool." It combines the sensual interior of the designer who makes the local atmosphere at a reasonable price with the food made with recipes that have been eaten and learned in Singapore for many years.

voyage.name: Oilje
voyage.content: The oilseed is freshly ground koshihikari rice. It is served with fresh rice, salted octopus, and GatKimchi. The oilseed seaweed soup is made of Geogeumdo-san young seaweed. You can dip seaweed in a special sauce and taste it stronger.

voyage.name: BaekGyeong restaurant
voyage.content: This restaurant is where you can feel the savory charm of juicy pork belly. It is a popular restaurant among residents.

voyage.name: Muswi
voyage.content: The natural light and wood-tone interior that come through the barrel create a warm atmosphere. There are different menus such as mushroom hamburger steak, tomato burrata pasta, and green onion pizza, and there is a lot of wine, so it is good to enjoy with food.

voyage.name: Beomyuda Samgakji
voyage.content: This restaurant is a Mexican, Western-based fusion restaurant where you can enjoy various kinds of alcohol and fusion Mexican food that you have never eaten anywhere.

voyage.name: Sam Sam Sam
voyage.content: It is a San Francisco restaurant that contains the sentiment of the U.S. mainland. It is loved as a Yongsan restaurant that combines authentic Italian menus in your own style. It is a place where authentic San Francisco sensibility meets Yongsan's sophisticated atmosphere.

voyage.name: PPS
voyage.content: It is a handmade burger shop representing Yongsan, starting in 2021.PPS is a place where you experience the deep taste of hamburgers with fresh ingredients and sophisticated recipes.

voyage.name: KkeoGeo
voyage.content: This is a conceptual restaurant with Hong Kong cuisine, not just ordinary Chinese food. This place has unflattering dishes and great alcoholic beverages to go with.

voyage.name: JeongSeong Son Kalguksu
voyage.content: This place is a hidden kalguksu restaurant near Yongsan Station.It offers a variety of menus such as noodles and bibimbap, especially chewy noodles and thick soup.

voyage.name: Jacoby's
voyage.content: Offers a wide variety of burgers, arguably the best for the value, in Seoul. In an area often known as the foreigner ghetto, a popular area for expats who live just west of Itaewon.

voyage.name: Pattaya
voyage.price: Stir-fried rice and noodle dishes cost ₩13,000-18,000, while curry pots and stews can run over ₩30,000
voyage.content: Thai restaurant, and perhaps the best in Seoul. With a menu featuring nearly 100 different items, you're bound to find your favorite dishes and make some new ones, too.

voyage.name: Zelen
voyage.content: Fantastic Bulgarian restaurant featuring lots of stuffed everything - from tomatoes to mushrooms, peppers and chicken breasts. Well-worth it as it is unique to the dining landscape in Seoul.

voyage.name: Don Charly
voyage.hours: dinner hours, sometimes closed for lunch
voyage.content: Not a Tex-Mex place: the front of the menu is a Spanish-language rant on that issue. This little "hole in the wall" will be something different for a lot of people. Portions are small, but that enables you to try a wider variety. Huge tequila menu; the Agavero is strongly recommended for dessert.

voyage.name: Bless U
voyage.content: Another older expat haunt. You better be good with your pool game or you'll be waiting in a long line to go again. Darts are also available. They have great popcorn and decent draft beers.

voyage.name: Burn
voyage.price: Shots of whiskey from ₩20,000 up, cigars from ₩20,000 to ₩50,000, food too expensive to think about
voyage.address: 11 Hoenamu-ro, Itaewon 2(i)-dong, Yongsan-gu, Seoul, South Korea
voyage.content: Cigar bar with a huge selection of liquor, especially Scotch; live music almost every night; friendly, sociable place to meet other expats and Hal, the one-of-a-kind man who owns the place.

voyage.name: Dillinger's
voyage.content: Serves draught and bottled beers and good food. Wednesday night is Wing Night, where 10 wings go for ₩4,000. Sports played on a number of big screens, plus lounge/club upstairs.

voyage.name: Helios
voyage.content: Seedy hip-hop club with a bit of a reputation.

voyage.name: Hollywood
voyage.content: A sports bar with a pool table, darts, a golf arcade game and several TVs airing all kinds of sports (including Premier League matches and major sporting events). Reportedly Nigerians and American soldiers have been banned here.

voyage.name: Metro
voyage.content: A lot of older expats and many Koreans hit up this joint. Only one Korean beer on tap, but free pool. The front (or right side when you go up the stairs) seems to be for the expat crowd, while the back (the left door when you go up the stairs) seems to be more hof style for the Korean crowd. They have the typical range of snacks available and free peanuts for beer drinkers.

voyage.name: Old Town
voyage.content: This is the bar/club that gets full when all the bars close. It is at its busiest between 04:00 and 08:00. Hard to miss, as it'll be the place that has everyone lounging around in various states in the very early hours of the morning. Not for the faint-hearted!

voyage.name: The Rose & Crown
voyage.content: London-style pub with great fish and chips and interior decoration. Darts and sports on the big screen available.

voyage.name: Sam Ryan's Sports Bar & Grill
voyage.content: This is the best sports bar in Seoul for North American sports. It shows numerous sports throughout the year on replay, sometimes live. There are TVs everywhere including the restrooms! Darts in the corner. Kitchen is extraordinary, excellent menu. The drink selection is great, better than most in Itaewon besides the 3 Alley Pub. The English-speaking staff is friendly as well, they still run a tight ship though. A te

voyage.name: Seoul Pub
voyage.content: Cheap beer, good atmosphere, a pool table, darts and Guinness on tap. It is quite dingy though, and badly needs a renovation, so probably a place for a session rather than a quiet pint with the missus!

voyage.name: B1's
voyage.content: An electro house club.

voyage.name: Club Volume
voyage.content: House and trance club, a quite large and excellent crowd on weekends. It is the best and most upscale club in the neighborhood.

voyage.name: Del Disco
voyage.content: Reportedly a gay club.

voyage.name: Pulse
voyage.content: Gay dance club.

voyage.name: Craftworx
voyage.content: Find the NOXA bar and walk past it two or three stores down. No pool or darts, but the best on tap beer you'll find in Korea. Seriously.

voyage.name: Phillies
voyage.content: A bar and grill that has changed ownership several times. Beer prices are par and food is OK.

voyage.name: Dragon Hill Spa and Resort
voyage.price: This jjimjilbang eschews the usual sauna vs. stay distinction in favor of a simpler ₩12,000 for 12 hr access rule
voyage.content: If you have never been to a jjimjilbang then this is perhaps a good place to start. A little on the pricey side for a bathhouse but the premises is modern, gaudily theme-decorated and incredibly tourist-oriented. Extensive signage exists in English, Chinese and Japanese as well as dedicated multilingual staff, even in the dead of night. Has the usual array of spas, saunas, heated sleeping rooms and Korean restaurants

voyage.name: Hamilton Hotel
voyage.content: A landmark in the heart of the Itaewon shopping district. Nice rooms, stay here to help reduce culture shock.

voyage.name: Noble Hotel
voyage.content: The exterior looks old, but the interior is neat and tidy. It is very close to Yongsan Station and it is very easy to move to other places.

voyage.name: Grand Hyatt Seoul
voyage.content: Set amidst landscaped gardens with good views over the city. Full service spa.

voyage.name: KBS Hall
voyage.content: Home of KBS Philharmonic Orchestra and KBS Traditional Music Orchestra.

voyage.name: 63 Building
voyage.content: This striking building was the tallest outside North America when it opened in 1985 at 250 meters. It has an art gallery and observation deck on level 60 that allows you to see far and wide over the city. As featured in the computer games SimCity 3000 and SimCity 4.

voyage.name: Korean National Assembly Building
voyage.content: The seat of the South Korean government and a work of contemporary architecture.

voyage.name: SeMA Bunker
voyage.content: A rather mysterious former bunker built during the 1970s military government. It was discovered in 2005 during the bus transfer center construction, and was opened as a gallery in 2017. It is part of the Seoul Museum of Arts.

voyage.name: Mullae Art Village
voyage.hours: Open area; individual studios and workshops have their own hours
voyage.content: A former ironworks district that has developed into an artists' village with studios, workshops, murals, outdoor sculptures, cafés, and restaurants. The narrow alleys preserve traces of the area's industrial history while displaying contemporary art. Many ironworks close on weekends, making the artwork painted on their shutters easier to see.

voyage.name: G Valley Industrial Museum
voyage.content: A museum documenting the history of the former Guro Industrial Complex and its transformation into today's Seoul Digital Industrial Complex. Exhibits include industrial products such as toys, televisions, radios, and other objects related to the area's manufacturing and labor history.

voyage.name: Netmarble Game Museum
